From c73cdbf804cf08fd8be83fcc4d6481f8fbc6a37d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Date: Tue, 17 Sep 2019 20:47:46 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915: Extend Haswell GT1 PSMI workaround to all

A few times in CI, we have detected a GPU hang on our Haswell GT2
systems with the characteristic IPEHR of 0x780c0000. When the PSMI w/a
was first introducted, it was applied to all Haswell, but later on we
found an erratum that supposedly restricted the issue to GT1 and so
constrained it only be applied on GT1. That may have been a mistake...

Bugzilla: https://bugs.freedesktop.org/show_bug.cgi?id=111692
Fixes: 167bc759e823 ("drm/i915: Restrict PSMI context load w/a to Haswell GT1")
References: 2c550183476d ("drm/i915: Disable PSMI sleep messages on all rings around context switches")
Signed-off-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Cc: Mika Kuoppala <mika.kuoppala@linux.intel.com>
Acked-by: Mika Kuoppala <mika.kuoppala@linux.intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20190917194746.26710-1-chris@chris-wilson.co.uk
(cherry picked from commit 56c05de6bd773b96deca379370965c49042b5fbf)
Signed-off-by: Rodrigo Vivi <rodrigo.vivi@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/intel_ringbuffer.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/intel_ringbuffer.c
index 601c16239fdf..bacaa7bb8c9a 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/intel_ringbuffer.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/intel_ringbuffer.c
@@ -1573,7 +1573,7 @@ static inline int mi_set_context(struct i915_request *rq, u32 flags)
 	struct intel_engine_cs *engine = rq->engine;
 	enum intel_engine_id id;
 	const int num_engines =
-		IS_HSW_GT1(i915) ? RUNTIME_INFO(i915)->num_engines - 1 : 0;
+		IS_HASWELL(i915) ? RUNTIME_INFO(i915)->num_engines - 1 : 0;
 	bool force_restore = false;
 	int len;
 	u32 *cs;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/intel_ringbuffer.c`**
   - The condition for determining the number of engines has been modified. 
   - The original line:
     ```c
     const int num_engines = IS_HSW_GT1(i915) ? RUNTIME_INFO(i915)->num_engines - 1 : 0;
     ```
     has been changed to:
     ```c
     const int num_engines = IS_HASWELL(i915) ? RUNTIME_INFO(i915)->num_engines - 1 : 0;
     ```
   - This change extends the PSMI workaround from being specific to Haswell GT1 to applying to all Haswell GPUs.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `intel_ringbuffer.c` is directly related to the bug fix described in the patch. The original restriction of the PSMI workaround to only Haswell GT1 was identified as potentially erroneous, leading to the broader application of the workaround to all Haswell GPUs. This change aims to address GPU hangs observed in Haswell GT2 systems, indicating that the previous limitation may have been too restrictive and not reflective of the actual issue affecting multiple Haswell configurations.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
const int num_engines =
-		IS_HSW_GT1(i915) ? RUNTIME_INFO(i915)->num_engines - 1 : 0;
```
```c
+		IS_HASWELL(i915) ? RUNTIME_INFO(i915)->num_engines - 1 : 0;
```
Reason:
The original code restricts the PSMI workaround to only Haswell GT1 systems, which led to GPU hangs on Haswell GT2 systems that were not accounted for. By checking only for GT1, the code fails to apply necessary workarounds for other Haswell configurations, resulting in unhandled GPU states.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
+		IS_HASWELL(i915) ? RUNTIME_INFO(i915)->num_engines - 1 : 0;
```
Reason:
This change extends the PSMI workaround to all Haswell GPUs, including GT2, ensuring that the necessary context handling is applied universally across all Haswell configurations. This prevents the GPU hangs that were previously observed on GT2 systems.
